title: Baghdad's knowledge boom
question: How did one empire turn translation into a golden age of learning?
hook: The top translators in Baghdad earned salaries estimated to rival those of today's professional athletes.
idea: The Islamic Golden Age grew from heavily funded translation of classical works, carried out by scholars of many backgrounds and helped by easy-to-make paper.

beats.prompt: Put these moments in the order they happened.
items: Harun al-Rashid reigns and the House of Wisdom is established
The Siege of Baghdad ends the Abbasid caliphate
The metaphor of a golden age is applied in literature on Islamic history
beats.explain: Harun al-Rashid ruled 786 to 809, paper reached Al-Andalus in the 10th century, the siege came in 1258, and the golden age label appeared in the 19th century.

beats.prompt: The caliphs' empire pays top translators very well and funds a large Translation Movement. What happens to ancient works from Greek, Persian, and Sanskrit sources?

choices.label: They are translated into Syriac and Arabic, saving works that might have been lost
Only Greek works are copied, and the rest are ignored
choices.feedback: Greek names stand out, but works were translated from Greek, Syriac, Middle Persian, and Sanskrit.

choices.label: They are locked away in the palace library for good
choices.feedback: Libraries do guard books, but some of these translations were later translated again into Hebrew and Latin.

beats.explain: Many classic works that might otherwise have been lost were translated into Syriac and Arabic, and some were later translated into Hebrew and Latin.

beats.prompt: Match each person or group to their part in the golden age.
pairs: Christian physician who led the House of Wisdom
Christian dynasty of physicians to the caliphs
Translated Greek philosophers into Syriac, then Arabic
A notably high proportion of the scientists
beats.explain: Christians and Persians both did major work in the golden age, in translation, medicine, and science.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning about who built the golden age is wrong. Which?
steps: The Islamic Empire heavily patronized scholars.
Many House of Wisdom scholars were Christian, and many scientists were Persian.
So the golden age was the work of a single group.
So paid translation helped it grow.
beats.explain: Christians and Persians both contributed greatly, so it was not the work of a single group.
